question: Should iOS opt into the durable transcript and spoken-confirmation capability now, after receiving real iOS proof that the gate and session continuity work on the merge head?
rationale: The merged gateway protocol deliberately preserves legacy-client behavior until a client advertises voice-transcript; enabling it in iOS changes the safety boundary for existing realtime voice calls.

options.title: Approve scoped iOS adoption after proof
options.body: Keep the advertised capability and merge after redacted simulator or device evidence demonstrates durable history, transport replacement, and a successful spoken-confirmation retry.

options.title: Defer iOS capability opt-in
options.body: Leave iOS on the legacy client behavior until the owner wants to schedule the confirmation-gate rollout separately.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped iOS adoption after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the advertised capability and merge after redacted simulator or device evidence demonstrates durable history, transport replacement, and a successful spoken-confirmation retry.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged gateway protocol and authored this client adoption, so they have the strongest context for the intended rollout boundary.
